literal: All matched the standards and largely followed ancient rites.
idiomatic: All matched standards and largely followed ancient rites.

literal: He had strong memory and silent retention, could decide great affairs, and whatever he created he handled without doubt.
idiomatic: He remembered silently, decided great affairs, and handled his creations without doubt.

literal: He was made General of Agile Cavalry and Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies, and rose in succession to Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He became General of Agile Cavalry, Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When gate officials were established he was Master of the Guard, middle grandee.
idiomatic: When gate offices were set he was Master of the Guard, middle grandee.

literal: When Emperor Ming ascended he was made Junior Director of the Ancestral Temples and advanced to Grand General.
idiomatic: Ming made him Junior Temple Director and Grand General.

literal: The emperor once visited his residence with the nobles—a scholar's glory.
idiomatic: The emperor once visited his house with nobles—scholarly glory.

literal: He went out as Yizhou inspector but, ill, did not take office.
idiomatic: Made Yizhou inspector, he did not take office for illness.

literal: He died; posthumous name Xian, with sacrifice in Wendi's temple.
idiomatic: He died, posthumous name Xian, with sacrifice in Wendi's temple.

literal: Son Shen inherited.
idiomatic: Son Shen inherited.

literal: Held the post of Fuzhou inspector.
idiomatic: He was Fuzhou inspector.

literal: Shen's younger brother Quan was quick and skilled at riding and archery, and held Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Brother Quan was quick, skilled at archery, and held Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: At the start of Sui Kaihuang, for Bian's fame in earlier ages he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Shen.
idiomatic: Kaihuang posthumously enfeoffed him Duke of Shen for earlier fame.

literal: Earlier, Zhou Wendi wished to implement the "Offices of Zhou" and ordered Su Chuo to oversee it.
idiomatic: Wendi wished to implement the Offices of Zhou and ordered Su Chuo to oversee it.

literal: Before long Chuo died and Bian was ordered to complete it.
idiomatic: Chuo soon died and Bian was ordered to finish.

literal: Thereupon by the "Rites of Zhou" six ministries were built, reforming Han and Wei law.
idiomatic: By the Rites of Zhou six ministries were built, reforming Han and Wei law.

literal: In the third year of Wei Gongdi it was first ordered implemented.
idiomatic: Wei Gongdi year three it was first implemented.

literal: Outside the six ministers were placed one Grand Preceptor, one Grand Tutor, and one Grand Protector each—the so-called Three Solitaries.
idiomatic: Outside the six ministers stood one Grand Preceptor, Tutor, and Protector—the Three Solitaries.

literal: The Eastern Palace was not yet built; crown prince offices were still being created.
idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was not built; crown prince offices were unfinished.

literal: Soon Canon-Making was changed to Grand Director of Rites, with a middle grandee.
idiomatic: Soon Canon-Making became Grand Director of Rites with a middle grandee.

literal: From then on each generation had additions and cuts.
idiomatic: Each generation thereafter added and cut.

literal: In Wucheng year one four Imperial Rectifiers were added, rank senior grandee.
idiomatic: Wucheng 1 added four Imperial Rectifiers, senior grandee rank.

literal: In Baoding year four Director of the Ancestral Temples became Grand Counselor, Rites Bureau became Director of Sacrifices, Grand Director of Rites became Rites Bureau, Grand Director of Music became Music Bureau.
idiomatic: Baoding 4 renamed temple director to Grand Counselor and reshuffled rites and music bureaus.

literal: In year five each Left and Right Martial Bearer gained one grandee.
idiomatic: Year five each Martial Bearer office gained a grandee.

literal: In Jiande year one palace guard offices were reorganized.
idiomatic: Jiande 1 reorganized palace guard offices.

literal: In year two the six ministries' bureaus cut all offices below middle grandee; each ministry kept four bureaus, with junior grandee as head and gentleman as deputy.
idiomatic: Year 2 cut offices below middle grandee; each ministry kept four bureaus headed by junior grandee with gentleman deputy.

literal: That year Eastern Palace offices were also expanded and changed.
idiomatic: That year Eastern Palace offices were expanded.

literal: In year three Remonstrating Counselors to the Crown Prince were first set, four posts, and ten Literary Scholars.
idiomatic: Year 3 first set four Crown Prince Remonstrating Counselors and ten Literary Scholars.

literal: Imperial younger brothers' and princes' Friends, two each, and six Academicians.
idiomatic: Princes' Friends, two each, and six Academicians.

literal: In year four palace guard offices were again reorganized.
idiomatic: Year 4 again reorganized palace guard offices.

literal: Offices like Martial Affairs and Palace Guard were all later additions.
idiomatic: Martial Affairs and Palace Guard were later additions.

literal: Eastern Palace chief steward and the like were also later creations.
idiomatic: Eastern Palace stewards were later creations.

literal: Yet statutes scattered and perished and cannot be fully known.
idiomatic: Statutes scattered and cannot be fully known.

literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he did not follow antiquity; office ranks and grades changed at whim.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuan ignored antiquity and changed ranks at whim.

literal: As for first setting the Four Assistants, restoring middle grandees in the six ministries, and adding senior grandees to Imperial Rectifier and Palace Scribe—these are now recorded in the external histories.
idiomatic: First Four Assistants, restored middle grandees, and added senior grandees are recorded in external histories.

literal: The rest changed morning and evening and cannot be fully recorded.
idiomatic: The rest changed daily and cannot be fully recorded.

literal: At the time, though the "Rites of Zhou" operated, inner and outer posts also used Qin and Han offices; here titles and rank numbers are briefly listed at left.
idiomatic: Though Zhou rites operated, Qin and Han offices remained; titles and ranks are listed at left.

literal: If the annals mention other offices not listed here, that too is the historian's omission.
idiomatic: Other offices in the annals but not here are historiographical gaps.

literal: Pillar of State and Grand General—in Jiande year four Superior Pillar and Superior Grand General were added.
idiomatic: Jiande 4 added Superior Pillar and Superior Grand General.

literal: Correct ninth rank.
idiomatic: Correct ninth rank.

literal: General of Agile Cavalry and Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies—in Jiande year four changed to Grand General Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies, with Superior added;
idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry and Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies became Grand General Privilege Equal, with Superior added in Jiande 4;

literal: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies—in Jiande year four changed to Grand General Privilege Equal, with Superior added;
idiomatic: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Privilege Equal became Grand General Privilege Equal, with Superior added;
